mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which elevates input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such sustained industrial production declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary inflation and rate-hike regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation with restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such housing starts recoveries.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs alongside a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 6% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses corporate earnings and investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained sub-1% annualized GDP growth.
